text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The caretaker government has decided to abandon "all wasteful projects and expenditures" to reduce heavy budget deficit.
- Pakistan refused to host a U.N. conference on Afghanistan scheduled for December 2-3 due to India's participation.
- The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees put most of its activities in Kabul on hold because of arrests and intimidation of its staff by the ruling Taleban forces.
- At least $100 million just vanished in a $1.0 billion submarine deal with France finalised by former Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, the Wall Street Journal said.
- The government has no plans to probe into foreign currency accounts of citizens inside or outside the country, a Finance Ministry spokesman said.
- The European Union has slapped anti-dumping fines ranging between 17 and 35 percent on Pakistani exports of unbleached cotton fabrics thus causing a loss of $180 million to Pakistan.
- The caretaker government will soon float $350 million Samurai Bonds in Japan to improve its balance of payments position, sources said.
- The state-run Corporate Law Authority said listed companies in Pakistan will be allowed to purchase their own shares.
- Mujadid Mirza, a retired judge of the Supreme Court, has been appointed as Accountability Commissioner to receive complaints against corrupt officials and politicians.
- President Farooq Leghari will announce a comprehensive structural reform package by December 20.

- Hashoo Group of Companies has served a legal notice to the government for cancelling the ousted cabinet's decision to allow the company to Burmah Castrol's shares in state-run Pakistan Petroleum Limited.
- About 35 Pakistanis are prisoners of former Afghan defence minister Ahmad Shah Masood in the Panjsher valley, Western journalists who travelled to Panjsher said.
